curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: Unnamed `""`; yank `"0`; numbered `"1`–`"9`; named `"a`–`"z`; append with `"A`–`"Z`; black-hole `"_`; small delete `"-`; clipboard `"+`; `p P gp gP`; `:registers` as inspection
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Preserve yanks, select storage deliberately, reuse multiple snippets, and understand why delete/change affects later puts
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Delete without overwriting a yank; paste the previous yank after another edit; collect lines into a named register; choose where to put text and where the cursor should land
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core through named and black-hole registers. The useful but host-dependent `"+` clipboard is emulated inside each Vim Wilds exercise and never touches the device clipboard

lessons.title: Understand the unnamed register
lessons.objective: See how yank, delete, and change feed the default register used by an unprefixed put.

activities.title: Every capture has a default home
activities.body: Yank, delete, and change store text in the unnamed register. Plain `p` and `P` read that current value, so a later edit can replace what you expected to put.
activities.grammar: operator → unnamed register → p or P
activities.contrast: The explicit name is `""`, but ordinary puts use it automatically.

lessons.title: Choose the put side and landing
lessons.objective: Distinguish before versus after placement from where the cursor finishes.

activities.title: Placement and landing are separate choices
activities.body: Lowercase `p` puts after the cursor or line; uppercase `P` puts before. Prefix either with `g` to finish just after the inserted text, which is useful when the next edit should continue there.
activities.grammar: p/P = side · gp/gP = side plus cursor after
activities.contrast: The inserted text is identical; only placement and final cursor differ.

activities.title: Large deletes form a history
activities.body: Linewise and multiline deletes enter register one. Each later large delete shifts older entries toward registers two through nine, giving you a short recovery stack.
activities.contrast: Numbered history is newest-first; it is not the same as yank register zero.

lessons.title: Use and inspect clipboard storage
lessons.objective: Practice the transferable plus-register command without exposing or depending on the device clipboard.

activities.title: The clipboard command stays inside the exercise
activities.body: In Vim and Vim integrations, `"+` addresses the host clipboard. Vim Wilds uses the same command grammar but stores its value only in the current exercise, alongside every other emulated register.
activities.contrast: Reset clears it, and no lesson reads or modifies the phone, tablet, or desktop clipboard.

lessons.title: Choose the right register and put
lessons.objective: Select storage and placement from the edit's actual risk and desired continuation point.

activities.title: Choose storage by what must survive
activities.body: Use the unnamed register for immediate work, zero to preserve a yank, numbered or small-delete history for recovery, black-hole for disposal, a name for planned reuse, and plus for clipboard-oriented transfer. Then choose the put variant by side and cursor landing.
activities.grammar: survival need → register · placement need → put
activities.contrast: The shortest command is not useful if it destroys the text needed next.
